subject: Variant compatibility overlap & temporary pin for peregrine-v2b
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@peregrine.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Peregrine v2b - artifacts + early compatibility notes

Hi Mina / team,

Thanks again for the intake call earlier — attaching the v2b artifacts and a short compatibility notes PDF. High level: this variant introduces a tokenization tweak and an optional fused-attention path that improves throughput on Ampere-class GPUs. We ran basic spot checks against the Redwood sample prompts (included) and saw a small drift on safety prompts (false positives increased ~1.2 percentage points).

Can you advise on how you prefer we handle a temporary pin vs letting the model go straight into canary? Peregrine prefers a conservative rollout while we validate inference parity across your kernel selection.

Attachments:
- peregrine-v2b-artifacts.tar.gz (model weights, config)
- compat_report_peregrine-v2b.pdf (short summary)
- sample_prompts_peregrine.csv

I can be on standby this week for any tests you want us to run.

Thanks,
Sara Liu
Head of Integrations, Peregrine AI

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine v2b - artifacts + early compatibility notes

Hi Sara — appreciate the quick handoff and the artifacts.

Short answer: we should do a temporary pin for peregrine-v2b in hosted canary while we run the extended compatibility suite. The tokenization change is the key risk here; it can cause subtle embedding drift and affect downstream rerankers.

Action items for our side (I’ll coordinate):
- Dev: run full compat matrix (tokenization parity, KV cache artifacts, fused-attn path fallbacks) across our Ampere and Hopper pools.
- Product: define the telemetry gating thresholds for safety drift and embedding cosine shifts.
- Integrations (Sara): provide a quick script to reproduce your internal checks and any deterministic seeds used.

If we lock a temporary pin we can prevent auto-roll into general pool until we validate. Karthik — want to weigh in on the threshold definition and whether this merits a special SLA clause for the canary window?

Mina
Director, Model Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@peregrine.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T15:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine v2b - artifacts + early compatibility notes

Putting preliminary test plan here. Will run overnight on staging:
1) Tokenization parity: run token-by-token compare on 10k sentence sample (Sara's sample + Redwood corpus).
2) KV cache stress: emulate long-chat sequences to ensure no drift when using fused-attn fallback.
3) Latency matrix: measure p95/p99 across Ampere/Hopper point types with fused-attn enabled and disabled.
4) Safety eval: run Redwood safety harness and our e2e prompt set; produce ROC curve and delta vs baseline.

If any of the safety metrics exceed +0.8 percentage points false positive or if embedding cosine distance > 0.02 on key customer prompts, propose we hold pin. I want product to confirm those numbers.

Also: will need a temporary variant pin API call — Mina, can you open the pin request and specify the intended max window? My preference is 14 days with auto-review at day 7.

– Dev
Senior Infra Engineer

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@peregrine.ai>
Date: 2028-06-29T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine v2b - artifacts + early compatibility notes

Thanks — I agree with Dev's thresholds as starting points but suggest one tweak: for safety drift we use a two-tiered approach.
- Tier 1 (block rollout): false positive delta > 1.0 ppt OR embedding cosine shift > 0.03 on any customer-critical prompt set.
- Tier 2 (hold & monitor): 0.5 ppt < delta <= 1.0 ppt OR 0.015 < cosine shift <= 0.03. In Tier 2 we can still release to an isolated dedicated pool with notification to impacted accounts.

Given Peregrine's note about a 1.2 ppt FP increase in their spot check, I'm inclined to approve a temporary pin until we run the full suite. Suggest pin window: 14 days with automatic review and mandatory telemetry export to Peregrine if we see Tier 2 flags. Grace — can Redwood Console support the telemetry export (sanitized) for this partner?

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Model Serving

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@peregrine.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine v2b - artifacts + early compatibility notes

Approving temporary pin as requested. Conditions:
- Pin duration: 14 days starting 2028-06-30 with auto-review on day 7.
- Telemetry export: we will provide a sanitized telemetry bundle (trace ids, token deltas, aggregated safety metrics) once daily to the Peregrine integration mailbox. No raw PII or full prompts to be exported — filtered per Legal's recommended template. Laura will own the export pipeline.
- If Tier 1 is hit at any point, pin remains until remediation and sign-off by Product + Security.

Laura: please coordinate the export template with Sara and get Legal looped for the filter rules. Dev: start the compat matrix and upload intermediate artifacts to the Drive link. Mina: I'll log the temporary pin in the release control board and notify Sales to pause any broad announcements.

Thanks all — good plan.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
